scope: The TOPPBase lifecycle of the independently versioned OpenMS4-cli package: command-line parse closure, INI merge and strict update, write commands and -write_ini parity, usage text, file and format checks, phase-aware exit codes and the run services (progress log type, thread policy, test-mode unique-id seed, processing annotations), and the processing records the ported tools attach to their outputs (decision D4). Package CLI-1 (C4-CLI-SPEC plus integrator step W1.4) and package CLI-2 (integrator step W2.2). Deliberately not resolved against the Core SDK checkout, except for the Param::update, StringUtils, TextFile, XMLFile, IndentedStream, ConsoleUtils and MzMLHandler behaviour the lifecycle and its comparisons reproduce.
method: TOPPBase.cpp and TOPPBase_test.cpp read at the cli pin and the five tools' sources at the topp pin with git show; generic cases executed against the C++ product SDK binaries DTAExtractor and SpectraFilterWindowMower by ../oracle/topp-cli-lifecycle/run.sh in a clean environment (env -i, per-case HOME and cwd, OPENMS_DISABLE_UPDATE_CHECK=ON, OPENMS_DATA_PATH=<sdk>/share/OpenMS/4.0.0); the Rust suite asserts each case's exit code and a diagnostic line, and compares the subsection-override output canonically with the C++ output. The INI read failures (an unreadable file, a directory, the character device /dev/null, a FIFO with mode 000, a Unix socket and /dev/tty without a controlling terminal, before a run and with -write_ini) were executed the same way by ../oracle/topp-cli-lifecycle/ini_read_failures.sh, which also records, as an observation, the C++ tool blocking on a FIFO whose only writer opens it once. Package CLI-2 executed ../oracle/topp-cli-lifecycle/cli2_cases.sh on the five ported tools' product SDK binaries: -test -write_ini of each tool (compared line by line with exact numbers and only version lines skipped, and as decoded parameter trees), --help and --helphelp of each tool (compared byte for byte after the stty line of the console-width probe is dropped and the revision in the version line is replaced), input format detection by name and content and output extension checks (exit code and diagnostic), and the registered BaselineFilter, MapNormalizer, SpectraFilterWindowMower and MzMLSplitter test invocations with and without -test (processing records compared as decoded mzML). The retained TOPPBase_test_write_ini_out.ini and TOPPBase_test_write_ini_subsec_out.ini are compared with the ported FuzzyStringComparator at TEST_FILE_SIMILAR's default tolerances and WHITELIST("version"). TOPPBase_test.cpp sections that apply to the native API are transcribed with their literals.
evidence_tier: oracle-generated (tier 1 executed differential) for the tool cases, including the INI read failures of ini_read_failures/manifest.json and the CLI-2 cases of cli2/manifest.json; tier 1 retained C++ output for the TOPPBase_test -write_ini files and for the processing records of the retained BaselineFilter, MapNormalizer, SpectraFilterWindowMower and MzMLSplitter outputs; source review (tier 3) for the transcribed TOPPBase_test.cpp sections; Rust-only (tier 4) for run_io routing, the run-phase mapping of every Error variant, the registration failure, the argument bound, the order of trailing-text chunks and a FIFO as -ini read once by a single writer (a deliberate difference; the C++ tool blocks, oracle observation write_ini_ini_fifo_single_writer). docs/TOPP_CLI_SUPPORT.md labels every exit-code row with its asserting test and tier.

oracle.reproducibility: run.sh: two executions agreed on exit code and every output sha256 for all 37 shared cases; ini_common_top_level ran once. ini_read_failures.sh: each time cases were added (device, FIFO, then socket, tty and the single-writer observation) the earlier cases ran again and matched in exit code, stderr and outputs; only the timing figures in ini_readable_control's stdout changed. cli2_cases.sh: two executions (cli2/manifest.json and cli2_rerun_manifest.json) agreed on every exit code and stderr of all 34 cases and on every output except the three non-test mzML outputs, which differ only in their completion-time lines; stdout differs only in timing figures. The retained fixtures come from the first execution.
